own.claim: Government recognition programs in India typically take weeks to months to complete examination; a single status update does not indicate urgency or imminent decision.
own.why: These processes involve multiple stakeholders and compliance checks; the timeline is set by the agency, not by the applicant's needs.

own.claim: When a government body moves an application to 'Under Examination,' the applicant should wait for the next communication unless the agency explicitly requests additional documents or information.
own.why: Proactive follow-up before a decision is made typically delays the process and signals uncertainty about the application's strength.

own.claim: Recognition from StartupSetu is a credential that supports fundraising but is not a blocker to raising; many successful seed rounds close without it.
own.why: Investors value traction and team more than government recognition; the credential is a plus, not a requirement.

patterns.claim: Government recognition processes move in stages and communicate status updates; 'Under Examination' typically means the application has passed initial screening and is in substantive review.
A status update from a government body with no request for additional information signals the process is on track.
Silence from a government body after an application is submitted is common and does not indicate rejection; a status update is a positive signal.
